data.description:
## Description

What: Create a deliberate synthetic PR containing a known CodeQL-detectable security issue (e.g., an insecure deserialization pattern), confirm in-session that the CodeQL job fails and the PR is blocked from merge, then close (not merge) the synthetic PR and record the demonstration as a comment on epic 88d2-6756. Why: This is the distinct cc-1 / Probe-6 verification slice — runtime proof that the enabled gate blocks a real finding rather than merely being configured. Scope IN: synthetic PR creation, in-session gating confirmation, PR closure, epic-comment capture. Scope OUT: the rule enablement itself (draft-4), the CI jobs.


## Done Definitions

- A synthetic PR with a known CodeQL-detectable security issue causes the CodeQL check run to fail and the PR to be blocked from merge, observed in a live PR run ← Satisfies: sc-1 ← Validates Closure Check: "A deliberate test PR with a known CodeQL-detectable security issue (e.g., insecure deserialization pattern) blocks merge until the issue is fixed — verified in-session."
- The synthetic PR is closed without merging and the gating demonstration is recorded as a comment on epic 88d2-6756 ← Validates Closure Check: "A deliberate test PR with a known CodeQL-detectable security issue (e.g., insecure deserialization pattern) blocks merge until the issue is fixed — verified in-session."

## Considerations

- [Safety] The synthetic PR must be closed, never merged — the insecure pattern must not land on any branch.
- [Sequencing] This demonstration is only meaningful after the rules are enabled (draft-4) and the CodeQL job emits data (draft-1).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a security maintainer, I want a synthetic CodeQL-detectable PR to demonstrate gating then be closed, so that we prove the gate actually blocks unsafe merges.
